skills.name: Polynomial vocabulary
skills.wrong_turn: The degree of 3x²y⁴ is 6 (add the exponents), and the degree of 5 is 0, not 1.
skills.rule: A polynomial is a sum of terms axn with whole-number exponents; its degree is the highest exponent.

skills.name: Add & subtract polynomials
skills.rule: To add polynomials, combine like terms; to subtract, change every sign of the second one first.

skills.name: Monomial × polynomial
skills.rule: a(b+c)=ab+ac: multiply the monomial by every term.

skills.name: Multiply binomials
skills.wrong_turn: (x + 3)(x + 5) is not x² + 15. The outer and inner products, 5x and 3x, are part of the answer.

skills.name: Special products
skills.wrong_turn: (x + 3)² is not x² + 9. The middle term 6x is always there.

skills.name: Multiply polynomials
skills.wrong_turn: Don't stop after the first term: x²(x + 2) is part, but −3x(x + 2) and 1(x + 2) are needed too.
skills.rule: Multiply each term of the first polynomial by each term of the second, then combine like terms.

skills.name: GCF factoring
skills.wrong_turn: When a term is the GCF itself, 1 remains: 3x² + 3x = 3x(x + 1), not 3x(x).
skills.rule: Factor out the greatest common factor: ab+ac=a(b+c).

skills.name: Factor by grouping
skills.wrong_turn: The binomials must match exactly: x²(x + 3) − 2(x − 3) has no common factor. Watch the sign when a pair starts with a negative.
skills.rule: Group terms in pairs, factor each pair, then factor out the common binomial.

skills.name: Factor x² + bx + c
skills.wrong_turn: Check the signs by multiplying: (x + 4)(x − 3) = x² + x − 12, not x² − x − 12.

skills.name: Factor ax² + bx + c
skills.wrong_turn: With a ≠ 1, you can't just find two numbers that multiply to c: 6x² + 7x − 3 is not (x + 9)(x − 2) or similar.
skills.rule: For ax2+bx+c, find m,n with mn=ac and m+n=b; split bx into mx+nx, then group.

skills.name: Difference of squares
skills.wrong_turn: a² + b² does not factor over the reals: x² + 9 is not (x + 3)(x + 3) or (x + 3)(x − 3).

skills.name: Perfect square trinomials
skills.wrong_turn: x² + 6x + 9 is (x + 3)², but x² + 9 isn't a perfect square: the middle term 6x is required.

skills.name: Sum & difference of cubes
skills.wrong_turn: x³ − 8 is not (x − 2)³. That expands to x³ − 6x² + 12x − 8.

skills.name: Factor completely
skills.wrong_turn: Check whether a factor factors again: 2x³ − 18x = 2x(x² − 9) isn't finished. It's 2x(x + 3)(x − 3).
skills.rule: GCF first, then a pattern, then keep factoring until every factor is prime.

skills.name: Polynomial division
skills.wrong_turn: Include a 0 for every missing power: dividing x³ − 5 needs coefficients 1, 0, 0, −5, not 1, −5.

steps.a: check an identity by expanding both sides
